I fixed it in `anthrouter/handlers.py`, but I haven't reproduced your exact sonnet-then-opus sequence or added a test for it. The full suite gives 1119 passed, 1 skipped and 1 failed. The failure is `tests/test_config.py::test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields`, which fails the same way with my change stashed, so it isn't caused by this fix.

**Cause:** the router remembers the tier it picked for a conversation and replays it on later turns that carry no fresh user text (tool-result turns and bare "yes"/"proceed" turns). That memory was keyed only by session plus the conversation's first message, not by which model the client asked for. Your `claude-sonnet-5-5` turn was classified `trivial` and routed to haiku, which was stored under that shared key. The later `claude-opus-5-5` turn in the same conversation then replayed the stored haiku. The tool-result and affirmation replays also skip the "never upgrade above what was requested" cap. Even where the cap does run, it deliberately lets a cached lower tier downgrade a higher request, so opus still dropped to haiku.

**Fix:** in `_prepare`, the tier-cache key now includes the requested model's tier (haiku, sonnet, opus or fable). A tier cached from a sonnet turn is only replayed for sonnet requests, so an opus turn can't inherit haiku from it. The other per-conversation state (context-size tracking) keeps the original key.

One side effect: a conversation that switches requested model mid-way no longer carries its routing memory across the switch. An opus turn that arrives with no fresh text after a sonnet turn will now get the normal fallback routing instead of inheriting the sonnet turn's tier.
